title: Enhanced item
description: A piece of enhanced gear: a specific named artefact, a modification bolted onto ordinary equipment, a cybernetic augmentation, a droid part, or a consumable. This is deliberately not the equipment content type. Enhanced items share only a name and a provenance with mundane equipment; they have no list price, no weight, no armor class and no damage dice, and they are found or crafted rather than bought. What they do have — a rarity band, an attunement requirement, a prerequisite, and the kind of item they attach to — is exactly what mundane equipment does not. Folding the two together would make eleven of equipment's fields conditional and would bury 507 shoppable rows under 1,918 rows with no price.

key.description: Stable slug identifying this item. Derived from the name once and never reused, so a character sheet keeps resolving after a rename.

name.description: Display name as printed. Many names carry a parenthesised grade — "Dispelling Dataport (Fine)" — because a modification is published once per grade rather than once with a table of grades.

sourceKey.description: Key of the source this item was published in, matching a document of the source content type. Every archived enhanced item comes from either wh or ec; the Player's Handbook has none.

contentSet.description: Whether this item belongs to the core rules or to the community expanded-content supplement.

itemType.description: What kind of enhanced item this is, and with it what a reader has to own before the item is usable. An itemModification is applied to a piece of equipment the character already has; a cyberneticAugmentation is grafted onto the character; a consumable is spent; the rest are worn or wielded. Over half the corpus is itemModification, which is why this and rarity are the two fields a list page cannot omit.

rarity.description: The rarity band, in ascending order. Rarity is the enhanced-item corpus's substitute for a price: nothing here carries a cost in credits, and rarity is what a table decides availability, crafting time and loot placement from. The enum order is the game's ladder, not alphabetical, so a schema-aware consumer can sort by it directly.

requiresAttunement.description: Whether a character has to attune to the item before its enhanced properties work. Always present, including when false, so a character sheet can count attunement slots without a null check.

subtype.description: The narrower kind, whose meaning follows from itemType. For an itemModification it is the equipment the modification is installed in ("wristpad", "vibroweapon", "clothing"); for adventuringGear it is the body slot the item occupies ("hands", "waist"); for a consumable it is what the thing is ("ammunition", "stimpac"); for a weapon it is the base weapon the enhanced version is built on ("bo-rifle", "sniper rifle"), or a whole family ("any blaster"). Fifty archived adventuring-gear entries record no slot at all, so the field is optional.

prerequisite.description: What the item needs before it can be used or installed, as printed: an ability score ("Constitution 13"), a class level ("At least 3 levels in berserker"), a droid class, or a property the host equipment must have or lack ("Lacks double or two-handed property"). Prose rather than structured conditions, because the printed clauses mix kinds freely and nothing downstream evaluates them yet.

description.description: Markdown giving the item's rules text, and sometimes a closing italic line of flavour. Always present: unlike equipment, an enhanced item with no text would have no effect.
